title: OpenAI ChatProxy: behavior preservation for streaming & function-call backcompat
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a conservative OpenAI Chat Completions proxy layer that preserves observable behaviors for legacy clients while mapping requests/responses onto Redwood's internal streaming + function-calling model. Focus on edge cases: partial function-argument streaming, delta vs final role/content semantics, stop-token preservation, chunk resequencing for SSE/http2, and deterministic idempotency tokens. Goal is feature-parity for existing OpenAI-style clients with minimal caller changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Legacy OA-cc clients can connect to the proxy with existing request shape and receive expected event frames for streaming (including function call fragments and final function call payloads)
2) No behavioral regressions for tool/function calling: partial args must be reconstructed and final function call payloads emitted exactly once per request
3) End-to-end integration tests covering reordering, truncated streams, retried connections, and duplicate fragments pass in CI
4) Telemetry: we emit mapping metrics (oa_request_id, mapped_model, mapped_variant, mapping_failures) and error rates remain below SLO targets during canary
5) Canary rollout plan exists and rollback is automated via console route policies
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff doc uploaded to Confluence https://confluence.redwood/inference/oa-chatproxy-behavior-preservation. Goal: surface edge cases that caused customer regressions in the last integration.

2025-02-14 - Liam Chen: Initial prototype for request normalizer submitted (branch: feature/ENG-711007-request-normalizer). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/4578. Prototype maps 'messages' and 'temperature' -> internal API but streaming framing is naive.

2025-02-18 - SRE review (Priya Singh): Raised concern about backpressure when reassembling fragments for large function args. Recommendation: stream-forward fragments to storage backend (kv-store) with a per-request shard and apply sliding-window reassembly to avoid head-of-line blocking.
2025-02-20 - Design feedback (Marco Alvarez): UX note - ensure that we pass through 'role' preservation in deltas for clients that depend on role transitions for UI (assistant->tool->assistant).
2025-02-22 - Security review (Nina Patel): Flagged that function call payloads may contain PII. We need explicit KMS tagging and audit log entry per final function call payload. Added to scope.
2025-02-25 - QA (Rita Gomez): Provided failing testcases for truncated SSE streams where partial json fragments arrive split across events. Added unit tests and a reproducible harness.
2025-02-28 - Liam Chen: Implemented delta-reassembly + de-dup idempotency token. Running canary in staging against legacy mobile clients. Early metrics look good; seeing <0.1% mapping failures.
activities: Spec: finalize mapping matrix from OpenAI ChatCompletions shapes to Redwood stream events and function invocation model
Implementation: request normalizer, streaming re-framer, partial-function-arg buffer + reassembly service
Security: KMS tagging and audit-log insertion for final function payloads
Testing: unit harness for split-chunk SSE, e2e with legacy clients, chaos tests for retried connections
Observability: add mapping metrics and per-request debug traces to Console
Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback threshold on mapping_failure_rate
design_decisions: Persist partial fragments to a per-request in-memory shard with LRU eviction; fall back to disk-backed buffer for >8MB payloads
Assign an 'oa_bridge_id' per incoming request derived from OA request id + timestamp to enable deterministic deduplication across retries
Preserve OpenAI's 'role' field in delta events but add a lightweight mapping header 'x-rw-oa-role' to aid internal routing
Emit function calls two-phase: stream intermediate 'fn_call_fragment' events, then a single 'fn_call_final' with complete args and signature
Do not attempt to strictly canonicalize user-supplied function schemas; instead validate and forward, failing fast with clear 4xx responses when invalid
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Head-of-line blocking when reconstructing large function args -> Mitigation: fragment streaming + sliding-window reassembly + size-based early flush to disk
Risk: Duplicate final function calls after network retries -> Mitigation: idempotency via oa_bridge_id and last-seen sequence index; write-once guard in buffer store
Risk: Security/PII exposure in logs -> Mitigation: redact partial fragments, only log final function payload with KMS envelope and audit entry
Risk: Client-side expectations about streaming tokens timing -> Mitigation: preserve timestamp delta metadata and document known clocking differences in migration notes
test_plan: Unit: reassembly engine with permutations of split utf-8 boundaries, SSE/data framing and backpressure conditions
Integration: legacy OA-cc client (v2.3) + proxy + Redwood runtime end-to-end using recorded transcripts from customer bug reports
Chaos: abruptly close stream at random offsets and assert that reconnect + resume yields correct single final function call
Performance: throughput test at 200 req/s with mixed short-chat and large-function-call workloads; ensure p95 latency within runtime-1.20 SLO
